newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - February 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - February 7.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.

- Ireland's opposition Fianna Fail leader Berti Ahern has deflected a challenge from the Prime Minister to go to the "senior Fianna Fail person who held high office" to seek the truth about reports that he received 1.1 million Irish pounds from Dunnes Stores.
- The Irish deputy Prime Minister, Dick Spring on Thursday night expressed the government's deep concern about the proposed loyalist march at Harryville, Ballymena, Northern Ireland tomorrow.
- The Irish pound has moved closer to the top of the ERM band as it continues to rise in tandem with sterling, leading to further difficulties for the Central Bank on the markets.
- A mother's battle for free education for her mentally handicapped son on Thursday forced the Irish government into a humiliating climbdown that will cost it millions of pounds.

- Many opposition Fianna Fail parliamentarians are worried that the Irish government's real motive in setting up the Dunnes payment tribunal is to "out' the former FF minister allegedly paid one million Irish pounds by Ben Dunne and cause maximum damage to the party in the run-up to the general election.
- Major skills shortages exist in the tourist industry, with 39 percent of employers experiencing recruitment difficulties, a new survey has revealed.
- With Ireland's credit growth still high, an increase in interest rates is inevitable in the short-term, a leading economist warneed on Thursday.
- Unemployment in Ireland has shown a significant decrease from 17 to 13 percent of the total workforce between 1993 and 1996.
- The Irish government is believed to be blocking a man named in the controversial Ben Dunne affidavit from locating an insurance company in Ireland.
- The Labour Court will today issue its crunch recommendtion aimed at averting Monday's first ever national strike by the country's 26,000 nurses as normal hospital services hang in the balance.
- Ireland's fomer prime minister Albert Reynolds on Thursday night accused the Irish and British governments of contributing by inaction to a deep crisis for the Northern peace process.

- Irish companies spent a record 2.4 billion Irish pounds acquiring other businesses at home and abroad last year, according to the annual review of mergers and acquisitions by Chapman Flood Corporate Finance.
